meta.about: Follow-ups that are not Advisory Actions: requests in the Final Reports (Conference committee reports, plus the board's, trustees' committees' and G.S.O. reports) dated for later (progress reports, drafts, items recommitted to a committee, other dated plans) and recommendations committed to the General Service Board (no date given), and what became of Advisory Action follow-ups once they fell due. Own-words summaries; refs "FRyy pP Lx-y" = report year, PDF page, line in the Drive text extract.
meta.sources: 2024-2026 Final Conference Reports (Drive, _GSC Explorer Data/text/reports); M-39 index in advisory_actions.json
meta.checked: Extracted 2026-10-21 by five range extractors, each adversarially verified, plus a completeness sweep of every 2027+/77th/brought-back mention in the 2024-2026 reports (workflow wf_a03fe14b-6c4). Excluded on purpose: items already in the Advisory Actions, recurring work with no date, facts shown elsewhere (Conference, Convention, Forum, REDELA/WSM dates; trustee rotations; budgets), recommendations not adopted, things already done.

requests.text: Proposed rewrite of the cost-per-group Q&A in “Self-Support: Where Money and Spirituality Mix” (F-3), giving 2025 estimates of GSO's cost per group and average group contributions.
Keep every Conference committee informed of all proposed agenda items as they arrive, through a quarterly PAI Status Grid.
Conference members should tell the Fellowship more clearly that the PAI cut-off covers only the next Conference and that submissions are welcome all year.
Swap the October feedback call for a joint trustees'/Conference committee meeting where everyone votes on PAI dispositions for the next Conference, with background shared beforehand.
Run the PAI Status Grid as an ongoing, curated list; an item stays on it until policy or the Joint Committee disposes of it.
Circulate working committee agendas ahead of the Joint Committee meeting so members see ongoing projects and annual review items.
Have the Conference affirm that its committees may raise items not on their agenda, or put off an item to a later Conference.
Hold a sharing session where trustees, directors, delegates and Staff discuss what each role does, building a common understanding of each one's scope and authority.

outcomes.text: The 76th Conference (April 26-May 2, 2026) met under the “Humility in Action” theme, which framed the opening remarks, keynote and sharing.
Three delegates gave the planned Sunday talks: restoration and grace with unity, “Gossip vs. Facts” on communication health, and finding common ground.
The Sunday workshop on “Keeping Our Own House in Order” was held in ten small breakout groups, sharing on Step Ten as applied to general service.
The Inventory Implementation Committee reported as a Conference committee; its 2031 five-year inventory cycle failed, and its PAI-process proposals were committed to the General Service Board.

C.P.C. committee reviewed an outline and project plan for the mental health professionals pamphlet, offered suggestions (e.g., adding a link to the Cochrane study) and wants a progress report or draft in 2027.
The C.P.C. committee accepted the AAWS LinkedIn page report; trustees had learned in February 2026 that Premium's hiring and job-search features did not serve the visibility goal.
The committee accepted AA Grapevine's new five-year plan, judging it aligned with Grapevine and La Viña purposes, and expects annual updates on performance metrics.
Progress was reviewed but the committee asked for a revised plan closer to the 2025 action, with two or more methods and low-cost delivery; progress due 2027, final report 2028.
The Literature committee discussed revised draft chapters of Living Sober, told the trustees to keep revising the same way, and wants a revised draft or progress report in 2027.
The revised “Understanding Anonymity” (P-47), now covering social media, was approved and retitled “Anonymity — Our Spiritual Foundation”; a cover QR code and 2024 survey footnote were requested.
Trustees' PI subcommittees sent a draft survey and implementation report; the Conference chose a pilot (up to $10,000) using the 2022 questionnaire instead of a full random-sample survey.
Report and Charter reviewed the board ad hoc committee's progress report, flagged overlapping categories and no formal definition of “founders,” and sent the topic to trustees' Literature for input.
Since 2025 the declaration centres on the Third Legacy of service and members’ part in the group conscience; the subcommittee was still working on it in 2026.
St. Louis was chosen; the Convention is set for July 4–7, 2030.
The General Service Board chose Indianapolis on October 30, 2023.
The 2026 committee moved the final survey report to the 78th Conference (2028); a progress report on a revised survey plan comes in 2027.
